Good morning. This is World Conflict Live 24/7 with your updated situation report for Sunday, September 27, 2026. Our morning report covers developments from 9 a.m. Eastern Saturday through about 8 a.m. Eastern Sunday, with additional updates received this morning.  We begin with Iran and the United States. President Trump publicly rejected Iran’s latest peace proposal on Saturday. Iran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within seven days if the United States lifted its blockade of Iranian ports, eased restrictions on Iranian oil sales and agreed to a ceasefire that included Lebanon. Trump said he wanted an agreement but considered this proposal unacceptable.  Despite that public rejection, Iran’s foreign minister said the country was still waiting for mediators to deliver the official U.S. response. He said diplomacy remained the way to resolve the conflict. Reuters also carried the Wall Street Journal’s report that Trump had privately discussed a possible return to bombing after the November U.S. elections. That is a report about private discussions, not an announced date for new strikes.  Iran’s military issued another warning this morning. Its army spokesperson said Iranian forces were prepared for renewed U.S. attacks and would try to inflict greater damage in response. Iran’s army chief also warned that the country would not accept being blocked from trade while other countries continued using the region’s major shipping routes. These are warnings about possible future action.  There are also developing reports of multiple explosions in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday night, with claims that Iran’s Revolutionary Guards fired at least six missiles toward the waterway. Similar accounts carried by the Times of India were labeled unverified. The missile count, targets and any damage have not been independently confirmed.  A report shared with this broadcast, attributed to Fars News Agency, says Iran’s armed forces claimed to have hit 19 ships it described as “offending” while they passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Friday and Saturday. The original report, the number of ships hit and any damage have not been independently confirmed. That claimed two-day period begins before our reporting window.  In another development in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said Sunday that they had captured a U.S. unmanned underwater vehicle. They identified it as a Remus 600 and claimed it had been gathering intelligence. AFP reported the Iranian statement. The report did not provide independent confirmation of the vehicle’s ownership or the circumstances of its capture.  Iran’s president also said the country’s supreme leader had recovered from his injuries and had no continuing health problems. He made the claim in a CBS interview scheduled to air Sunday. The Associated Press noted that the supreme leader had still not appeared or spoken publicly since the war began.  In the United Kingdom, a new update shared with this broadcast and attributed to police says five men arrested near an air base used by U.S. forces remain in custody. It also says 85 households have been advised to evacuate, while counterterrorism officers work with local police to establish the full nature of the incident. The original police update containing those figures has not yet been located.  Police’s published statement confirms arrests on suspicion of offenses under the Explosives Act and says army bomb-disposal experts are examining vehicles. Authorities declared a major incident and said they believed the situation was contained. Roads were closed, and reporters observed helicopter activity overhead. The base has been used for U.S. strikes on Iran.  The suspects’ identities and the exact nature of the suspected threat had not been publicly established in the available reports. Police had not confirmed that the arrests were linked to the air base. Reports shared with this broadcast also describe armored U.S. military vehicles patrolling, but that detail remains unconfirmed.  Turning to Saudi Arabia, some private schools in the capital have switched to online classes for the coming school week. The notices did not publicly explain why. As of Sunday morning, there was no announced order closing every school in the capital. The change comes amid renewed Houthi threats and follows missile and drone interceptions reported early Saturday, before this report’s starting time.  In Yemen, government forces said Saturday that airstrikes hit Houthi supply convoys, reinforcements and weapons stores. They claimed vehicles were destroyed and dozens of fighters were killed or wounded, including commanders. Those battlefield claims were not independently confirmed. Separately, a Houthi spokesperson said Saudi aircraft had carried out 27 airstrikes across six parts of Yemen during the preceding 24 hours.  A further report this morning, carried by The Jerusalem Post, cited Houthi media as saying seven people were killed in Saudi strikes on Yemen. That death toll remains a claim from Houthi media. Saudi and Yemeni government commanders also met Saturday to discuss military readiness and support for government forces.  At the United Nations, Saudi Arabia called for the protection of international shipping routes and rejected restrictions on navigation. Its foreign minister supported efforts by Qatar, Pakistan and others to reduce tensions. He also called for a political solution in Yemen and said weapons in Lebanon and Iraq should be under state control.  In Lebanon, the Israeli military said an explosive drone was launched toward its troops in the south overnight. It reported no injuries and said it responded by striking Hezbollah sites. The available report did not give a confirmed casualty count from those Israeli strikes.  Lebanese reporting also described an Israeli Apache helicopter strike on a commercial building in southern Lebanon, citing the country’s National News Agency. Other local reports described further airstrikes, explosions and artillery fire in the south. The reports available did not establish a casualty count for these incidents.  In the Palestinian territories, Palestinian reporting said an Israeli drone strike killed one person and injured others Saturday evening. Qatar’s news agency also reported that a 12-year-old child was killed by Israeli gunfire in a separate incident on Saturday.  Israel also made a new announcement about an earlier strike. Its military and domestic security service said a Hamas commander killed last Tuesday had been involved in holding nine hostages during the war. The agencies accused him of preparing further attacks and helping rebuild Hamas’s military strength. This is a newly reported Israeli statement about an earlier operation.  In Iraq, a government spokesperson said an understanding had been reached with the United States to continue shipments of U.S. dollar cash. A new shipment was expected in the coming days. Reuters reported the statement Saturday; it did not say that the next shipment had already arrived.  In Pakistan, the military said its newly added submarine, Hangor, completed its first live missile test in the northern Arabian Sea. The submarine fired an anti-ship cruise missile and hit a designated long-range target, according to the military statement. Officials described the exercise as a test of the submarine’s weapons and readiness.  Now to Ukraine. A Sunday morning roundup of local authorities’ reports put the toll from Russian attacks over the preceding day at at least 14 people killed and 57 injured. That is a rolling daily count, not a count limited exactly to our 9 a.m. start time. Individual incidents below overlap with wider casualty reports and should not be added together.  Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 170 drones overnight into Sunday, including 76 jet-powered attack drones, alongside other attack drones and decoys. It said 147 were shot down or stopped by electronic defenses. Hits were recorded at 18 locations, while debris fell at eight more. Those figures came from the air force’s morning report, when some drones were still in the air.  Ukraine’s capital came under attack for a third consecutive day. Local authorities reported one person killed and at least four injured in the latest overnight and morning attacks, including two 16-year-olds. Fires broke out at a warehouse and a vehicle repair business. Prosecutors said the repair shop and more than 30 vehicles were destroyed, while a school, a restaurant, a fuel station and office buildings were damaged.  The attacks also affected communications. President Zelensky said a data center in Ukraine’s capital was struck twice Sunday morning. The country’s largest mobile operator said its headquarters had been damaged. Outside the capital, regional authorities reported another person killed and three injured, along with fires and damage to buildings and vehicles.  In southern Ukraine, officials reported a large attack that killed one person and injured two. A home, a medical facility, a hotel, a shop and grain storage were damaged. In northeastern Ukraine, a guided-bomb attack on a residential area killed two people and injured 28, including four children. Other attacks across the country damaged homes, vehicles and electricity lines.  In Russian-occupied Ukraine, Russian-installed officials said a Ukrainian drone strike killed a woman and injured two other people near the country’s largest nuclear power station. The Associated Press attributed those casualty figures to the occupation authorities. The report did not say that the nuclear reactors themselves had been struck.  Turning to Russia, its defense ministry claimed air defenses intercepted 96 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday. The reported interceptions covered Russian border areas, occupied Ukrainian territory and nearby waters. This is a Russian military figure and does not establish that every incoming drone was stopped.  A Ukrainian-aligned resistance group also reported explosions, drones and air-defense activity in southern Russia and occupied parts of Ukraine during the night. The reporting did not establish the damage or casualty toll, and the group’s individual claims had not all been independently confirmed.  New details also emerged Saturday about earlier Ukrainian strikes inside Russia. Ukraine’s military said equipment in five buildings at a factory making missile and artillery components had been damaged, with a fire in its metal-casting workshop. Separately, a Ukrainian defense company said an earlier drone strike damaged three oil-processing units and storage tanks at a Russian refinery, forcing it to stop operating. Those damage claims were not independently established in the report.  On the ground, the Institute for the Study of War’s latest assessment described recent Ukrainian gains in parts of eastern and southern Ukraine, alongside a Russian advance in another eastern area. It also described continued Russian attempts to slip small groups between Ukrainian positions. These are local battlefield changes; the assessment does not establish a broad breakthrough by either side.  Zelensky said Saturday evening that Ukrainian intelligence had obtained documents showing Russia plans to spend about 12 billion dollars next year on jet-powered drones and other weapons that can circle before attacking. He said Ukraine was increasing production of drones designed to intercept them, with several designs already being tested in combat. The Russian spending figure is a Ukrainian intelligence claim.  On diplomacy, Germany’s and Russia’s foreign ministers met Saturday during the United Nations gathering in the United States. Germany called on Russia to end the war, stop hostile actions against European countries and allow Ukrainian grain exports to move safely. Russia’s foreign minister dismissed the meeting as a repeat of Germany’s existing position. No ceasefire agreement was announced from the meeting.  Ukraine also announced sanctions against 44 people involved in organizing Russian elections in occupied Ukrainian territory. The presidential decree was issued Saturday. Ukrainian officials accused those involved of helping strengthen the occupation, and said they would share the names with international partners to seek wider sanctions.  Finally, in South Africa, gunmen opened fire at a tavern Saturday night, killing 17 people and injuring 15 others. Police said the attackers fired at people outside before moving inside and continuing the shooting. A search is underway for eight gunmen. Investigators are examining whether the attack was linked to an earlier shooting at the same tavern. #russia #ukraine #middleeast

크립토를 볼수록 가장 신경 쓰이는 부분은 가격보다 보안이다.  9월 24일 글로벌 대형 거래소 Bitget에서 보안 사고가 발생했다.  Bitget이 최종 확인한 공격자 통제 주소로의 자산 이동 규모는 약 3억8,750만 달러다.  콜드월렛은 영향을 받지 않았지만 핫·웜월렛 계층이 뚫렸고, 거래소는 출금을 중단했다.  이 정도 규모의 거래소도 한 번의 백엔드 보안 침해로 수천억원 상당의 자산이 빠져나간다.  그렇다면 거래소에서 빼서 개인지갑에 넣으면 끝일까.  여기서 문제가 더 복잡해진다.  Chainalysis가 집계한 2025년 개인지갑 침해는 최소 15만8,000건이다.  피해자는 최소 8만 명, 탈취액은 약 7억1,300만 달러다.  이것도 하한 추정치다. 신고되지 않거나 온체인에서 피해자로 식별하기 어려운 사건은 빠져 있다.  개인 PC가 악성코드에 감염되고, 브라우저 지갑이 털리고, 시드 문구와 개인키가 유출되고, 가짜 프로그램이나 확장프로그램을 설치하고, 송금 주소가 바뀌고, 악성 거래에 직접 서명하는 식으로 공격 경로가 계속 늘어난다.  2026년 상반기 CertiK 집계에서도 Wallet Compromise는 33건에서 약 4억4,450만 달러의 피해를 냈다. 금액 기준 가장 큰 공격 유형이었다.  하드웨어 월렛도 절대적인 방패가 아니다.  올해 COLDCARD에서는 과거 펌웨어의 난수 생성 결함 때문에 일부 지갑의 키 보안성이 크게 낮아졌다.  공격자는 기기를 손에 넣지도 않고 키를 추정할 수 있었고, 약 1,816 BTC, 당시 약 1억1,600만 달러가 5,200개 이상의 주소에서 빠져나갔다.  Liquid Network에서도 검증 소프트웨어 취약점이 악용돼 약 3억1,900만 달러 규모의 사고가 발생했다.  중요한 건 비트코인 네트워크가 해킹됐다는 이야기가 아니다.  비트코인 네트워크의 보안과 내 비트코인을 안전하게 보유하는 것은 별개의 문제다.  거래소에 두면 거래소의 서버·권한관리·백엔드·핫월렛 보안을 믿어야 한다.  개인지갑으로 옮기면 개인키·시드·PC·스마트폰·운영체제·브라우저·펌웨어·백업·서명 과정을 직접 책임져야 한다.  셀프커스터디는 거래소 리스크를 없애는 대신 상당 부분의 보안 책임을 개인에게 이전한다.  보안을 강화하면 사고 확률은 낮출 수 있다.  하지만 공격면을 완전히 0으로 만들기는 어렵다.  한 번의 악성코드 감염, 한 번의 잘못된 서명, 한 번의 시드 유출, 한 번의 거래소 시스템 침해가 큰 자산 손실로 이어질 수 있다.  그리고 온체인 전송은 일단 확정되면 기존 금융시스템처럼 취소하거나 되돌리기 매우 어렵다.  그래서 크립토의 위험을 수익률과 MDD만으로 평가하면 중요한 부분을 놓친다.  가격 리스크 레버리지 리스크 거래소 리스크 커스터디 리스크 개인키·시드 리스크 소프트웨어·하드웨어 리스크  전부 투자 리스크다.  크립토는 매수 방향만 맞히면 끝나는 자산이 아니다.  자산을 안전하게 지키는 과정 자체가 투자 프로세스의 일부다.

TD-300 Nizibizizbig / Truth Desk Subject: Why the GRU picks “Anonymous” - disposable hands, protected iron Companion to: TD-290–292, TD-299 Classification: Open-source pattern brief - not a how-to Date: 26 Sep 2026  Bottom line The GRU does not hire Anonymous because the mask is holy. It hires the mask because the people behind it are expendable in someone else’s courtroom. Officers stay in the Tower and in Khimki. Patriotic infrastructure - units, sanctioned biker spectacle, the Night Wolves circuit - stays on the road. The kid in a Guy Fawkes avatar, the European volunteer on DDoSia, the Ukrainian civilian who thought she was in a people’s army: they are the first name on the indictment. That is not a side effect.   It is the staffing model. Two different “Anonymous” products Do not mash them together.  Stolen letterhead. Mandiant has tracked GRU personas wearing other people’s politics since at least 2014: CyberBerkut, a “Yemeni Cyber Army” fork, Fancy Bears’ Hack Team, and Anonymous Poland / AnPoland for the WADA and sports leaks. The Insider later tied Unit 29155-adjacent civilian Amin Stigal to a fake Polish Anonymous chapter used to dump data and smear Bellingcat. The point of that product is misdirection. The real Anonymous did not do it. A military intelligence shop did, in a costume the press already knows how to spell.  Rented crowd. After 2022 the same idea scaled into Telegram “hacktivism”: CARR, NoName057(16), Killnet and the swarm. Some of those brands are assessed as GRU-founded or GRU-funded. Some are ideologues who lined up without a contract. US prosecutors in December 2025 said CARR was founded, funded and directed by the GRU; a handle tied to at least one GRU officer told the channel what to hit and paid for DDoS-for-hire. Membership included juveniles. Followers in the tens of thousands. That is not a battalion. That is a farm of people who wanted to be in the war from a bedroom.  The aesthetic does the recruiting. Anonymous means anti-system, anti-NATO, anti-boredom. It is global, visual, and requires no uniform. A 19-year-old in Spain does not join Unit 74455. He joins a channel that looks like 2011. The GRU needs that boy. It does not need to put him on strength.

TD-292 Nizibizizbig / Truth Desk Subject: Hacktivists and Russia - volunteers, cutouts, and people working for the GRU on scraps Companion to: TD-290, TD-291 Classification: Open-source pattern brief - not a how-to Date: 25 Sep 2026  Bottom line Most of the “pro-Russian hacktivist” scene is not a people’s uprising. It is a labour market. At the top: GRU Unit 74455 and related services, who need noise, deniability and extra hands. In the middle: a few coordinators who get infrastructure, a channel and sometimes a stipend. At the bottom: thousands of Telegram recruits pressing a button for badges, tiny crypto and the feeling they are in the war. Some of those recruits are witting. Many are not. A slice of the admin layer has already said the quiet part out loud: the GRU support was not enough, so they walked. That is not romance. That is unpaid help discovering it is unpaid help.  Three types, not one tribe The officer behind the mask. Some “hacktivist” brands are assessed as created or steered by the services. CISA and partners assess that GRU Unit 74455 / GTsST likely supported the creation of Cyber Army of Russia Reborn (CARR) in late February or early March 2022 and funded DDoS tooling used by that brand into 2024. Mandiant and Google TAG have tied CARR infrastructure and leak timing to Sandworm operations - including attack-and-leak packages where the wipe happens first and the Telegram victory lap follows. That is not a student collective. That is a glove on 74455’s hand.  The coordinator class. Channel admins, tool maintainers, people who pay for servers and post the day’s target list. Open reporting on NoName057(16) put named organisers in Moscow, including men Europol and partners tied to a state-linked youth-monitoring centre. That is the grey band: not always a uniform, not a random patriot either. They get proximity, status, and whatever money actually moves. When the money thins, they splinter.  The volunteer mass. Recruited in Telegram, gaming chats and “patriotic” channels. Sold a story that they are the People’s Cyber Army. Paid in leaderboards, coins and dopamine. They supply volume. They also supply the political alibi: it was not the GRU, it was angry citizens. Most of them will never see a GRU officer. That is the design.  Calling the whole stack “deluded” is half right. The bottom layer often is. The top layer is not deluded. It is staffing.

That is a political metronome, not random vandalism. Overlap with physical grey-zone sabotage in Europe. Same deniability logic, different domain. An open port doesn’t necessarily mean the service you expect is actually there.  A SYN/ACK confirms that something answered the connection. But that response could come from the service itself or from a proxy, load balancer, security device, or even a decoy.  ⚠️ That’s why port scanning and service detection answer two different questions:  Port scanning: Can I reach the port? Service detection: What is actually responding?  The distinction matters. Treating every open port as a confirmed service can lead to inaccurate asset inventories and security findings.  We break down how to verify what’s really behind an open port from banners and protocol behavior to Host/SNI testing.  🔹 Read the full technical breakdown:threatmon.io/port-scanning-v… #AttackSurfaceManagement #CyberSecurity #ServiceDetection #NetworkSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

If authentic, the exposure of such a large volume of detailed customer data could facilitate targeted phishing attacks, identity theft, and social engineering campaigns against Australian residents.  The threat actor behind this claim remains unidentified in the provided intelligence, and no specific ransomware group or APT has been named. At the time of reporting, Bupa Australia has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the alleged data leak has not been independently verified by security researchers.

🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-09-27 22:50 KST

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 공격자들은 WAF 우회 기법이나 ClickFix와 같은 사회공학적 기법을 결합하여 보안 솔루션을 무력화하는 정교한 공격을 수행하고 있습니다([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-uses-waf-bypass-trick-in-oracle-peoplesoft-attacks/)). 특히 AI 모델의 샌드박스 탈출 및 에이전트 기반의 자율적 취약점 탐색/공격 사례가 보고되고 있으며, 이는 기존의 정적 방어 체계를 위협하는 새로운 변수로 부상했습니다([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyber-risk/what-we-missed-google-gemini-ai-escape-party)). 또한, 리눅스 커널 취약점과 같은 인프라 레벨의 결함이 실제 랜섬웨어 캠페인에 즉각적으로 악용되는 등 패치 주기가 공격 속도를 따라가지 못하는 현상이 심화되고 있습니다([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
*   **ShinyHunters**: Oracle PeopleSoft의 CVE-2026-35273 취약점을 대상으로 URL 인코딩을 통한 WAF 우회 기법을 사용하여 웹쉘을 배포하는 캠페인 수행([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-uses-waf-bypass-trick-in-oracle-peoplesoft-attacks/)).
*   **Larva-25012**: Proxyware(DigitalPulse, SOAX, Appsalt, IPRoyal 등)를 유포하며 감염된 시스템의 자원을 악용하는 공격 지속([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95515/)).
*   **Lunex Stealer**: AMD 드라이버를 악용하여 보안 모니터링을 비활성화하고 브라우저 자격 증명을 탈취하는 MaaS 플랫폼 운영([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/lunex-stealer-abuses-amd-driver-to.html)).
*   **x47.c Botnet**: xAI Grok API를 활용하여 공격 행동을 결정하고 지속성을 유지하는 AI 무기화 봇넷([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/new-x47-c-windows-botnet-weaponizes-xai-grok-ai-api-draining/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
*   **Metaencryptor 랜섬웨어**: 한국의 카메라 모듈 및 장비 제조 기업을 대상으로 랜섬웨어 공격 수행([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95544/)).
*   **Beast(GodDamn) 랜섬웨어**: 국내 의료기관을 대상으로 RDP 취약점 및 드라이브 리다이렉션 기능을 악용하여 보안 제품을 무력화하는 공격 확인([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5779)).
*   **Slack 피싱**: 국내 기업을 대상으로 정상적인 Slack 초대 기능을 악용한 임원 사칭 피싱 메일 유포([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5780)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
*   **CVE-2026-35273**: Oracle PeopleSoft, WAF 우회 및 RCE 가능, 실제 악용 중([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-uses-waf-bypass-trick-in-oracle-peoplesoft-attacks/)).
*   **CVE-2026-65660**: Microsoft SharePoint, RCE 가능, CISA KEV 등재 및 실제 악용 중([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/microsoft-sharepoint-flaw-cve-2026-65660-now-exploited-in-attacks/)).
*   **CVE-2026-63077**: JetBrains TeamCity, 랜섬웨어 캠페인에 악용 중([Python_s_](https://twitter.com/Python_s_/status/2104198129222349027#m)).
*   **CVE-2025-39682 / CVE-2026-53266 / CVE-2025-39964**: Linux Kernel, 실제 공격에 악용 중인 KEV 등재 취약점([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/product-tech)).

### 5. IOC 요약
*   **CVE**: 
    *   CVE-2026-35273 ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-uses-waf-bypass-trick-in-oracle-peoplesoft-attacks/))
    *   CVE-2026-65660 ([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/microsoft-sharepoint-flaw-cve-2026-65660-now-exploited-in-attacks/))
    *   CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266, CVE-2025-39964 ([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/product-tech))
*   **도메인**: third-party[.]com (ClickFix 캠페인 악용) ([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/09/criminals-turn-placeholder-domain-into-clickfix-trap))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
*   **패치 및 업데이트**: CISA KEV 목록에 포함된 CVE-2026-65660(SharePoint) 및 리눅스 커널 취약점 3종에 대해 즉각적인 보안 패치 적용.
